globalTriggers.name: autosave
globalTriggers.summary: Writes an autosave immediately, rotating the three autosave slots.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Nothing in the engine fires this trigger on its own; it exists so content can request an autosave at a chosen moment. It runs whenever a dialog effect, another trigger's trigger effect, an action effect that raises the trigger actor value, or a user-interface command names it.
firedBy: Dialog effects that name 'autosave', as the game's own fleet-battle dialog does
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Actions, via an effect that raises the trigger actor value with this trigger's name
User-interface commands that ask for a trigger by name

effects.description: Saves the game into the first autosave slot, after pushing the two newer autosaves down a slot and discarding the oldest. Because no save name is supplied, the save goes ahead even in hardcore mode, but it is still skipped while the global variable that blocks autosaving is set.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterCombat
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs whenever combat starts, so content can attach its own effects to the start of a battle.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires every time the game switches into combat, immediately after the combatants have been gathered onto the battlefield, with the actor that started the fight as the triggering actor. Only its requirement formula is consulted at this point, so it is not blocked by the once-per-zone done list and it fires again on every fresh battle.
firedBy: The engine, when combat begins
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it and have them run at the start of every battle.

globalTriggers.name: tExitCombat
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs whenever combat ends, so content can attach its own effects to the end of a battle.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the game leaves combat and returns to travel mode, whether the battle was won, lost or fled, once the party is back under travel controls and the travel music has resumed. It is skipped while a new game is being loaded. The player actor is the triggering actor, and only its requirement formula is consulted, so it is not blocked by the once-per-zone done list and fires again after every battle.
firedBy: The engine, when combat ends
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it and have them run at the end of every battle.

globalTriggers.name: tKill
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs the first time an actor the player does not control is knocked out, so content can react to kills.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when an actor that is not under the player's control is incapacitated for the first time, right after the game has added one to the running kill count for that actor's type. An actor that was already knocked out once does not fire it again, and knocking out one of the player's own crew never fires it. No actor is passed along as the triggering actor, so formulas in its effects have no subject to read from.
firedBy: The engine, when an uncontrolled actor is knocked out for the first time
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it and have them run on every kill.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterBoardingZone
globalTriggers.summary: Covers the transition into a boarding fight with a screen fade and arms the two triggers that end the boarding when the fight is decided.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires once the boarding-deck zone for the ship being boarded has finished loading, as the last step of setting that zone up. It runs no actor as the triggering actor.
firedBy: The engine, when a boarding deck is set up after one ship boards another
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Plays the short screen-blackening effect. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position and covers the whole view while the boarding deck appears.

Three tenths of a second after this trigger fires, copies the global trigger 'tEndBoarding_combatWon' into the boarding-deck zone so that winning the fight there ends the boarding. Nothing happens if the zone already has a trigger of that name. Because it is delayed, it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left before the delay elapses.

Three tenths of a second after this trigger fires, copies the global trigger 'tEndBoarding_combatLost' into the boarding-deck zone so that losing the fight there ends the boarding. Nothing happens if the zone already has a trigger of that name. Because it is delayed, it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left before the delay elapses.

globalTriggers.notes: Both flags only matter if a zone lists this trigger among its own triggers; when the engine fires it directly they are not consulted. Marking it as firing immediately on zone entry also means that walking into its area can never fire it.

globalTriggers.name: tBoardingZoneCombat
globalTriggers.summary: Starts the fight on a boarding deck and sets the countdown that will end the boarding.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires on a countdown that the engine starts while the boarding cut-scene plays: three seconds after the last boarder has finished climbing across, once everyone is aboard the target ship. It runs with no triggering actor.
firedBy: The engine, on a countdown started while the boarding cut-scene runs
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: A tenth of a second after this trigger fires, forces combat to begin at once, centred on tile 1,1 with a battlefield radius large enough to take in the whole deck, then queues the action 'endBoarding_act' to be cast on that same tile after 80 units of combat time, which is what eventually ends the boarding. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left before the delay elapses.

globalTriggers.notes: The 80 in this effect is a placeholder: when a boarding starts, the engine overwrites it with the boarding duration supplied by the action that launched the boarding, which defaults to 80 units of combat time. Changing the number here has no effect on ordinary boardings.

globalTriggers.name: tEndBoarding
globalTriggers.summary: Ends a boarding fight and puts the party back on the sea, wherever the fight has got to.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Nothing in the engine fires this trigger on its own. In the shipped game it is fired by the boarding countdown action, whose effect names this trigger, so it goes off when the boarding runs out of time. It can equally be fired by a dialog effect, by another trigger, or by a user-interface command.
firedBy: Actions, via an effect that raises the trigger actor value with this trigger's name, which is how the game's own boarding-timeout action ends a boarding
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Ends the boarding: blackens the screen, drowns any hostile boarders left in the water once no fighters remain, awards the party the experience earned from everyone knocked out during the boarding, sends the boarding party's crew back to their ship, leaves combat, and moves the player back to the zone the boarding started from. It does nothing at all if no boarding is in progress.

globalTriggers.notes: Does nothing unless a boarding is actually under way, so it is safe to fire speculatively.

globalTriggers.name: tEndBoarding_combatWon
globalTriggers.summary: Ends a boarding fight the moment the boarders win it.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when combat is won in a zone that carries this trigger. The boarding-deck setup puts it there: 'tEnterBoardingZone' copies this trigger into the deck zone shortly after the deck loads, so winning the fight on the deck ends the boarding. A trigger only reacts to a won battle once it belongs to the current zone, so on its own, as a global trigger, it never fires from the battle result.
firedBy: The engine, when a battle is won in a zone that carries this trigger
'tEnterBoardingZone', which copies this trigger into the boarding-deck zone
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Ends the boarding: blackens the screen, drowns any hostile boarders left in the water once no fighters remain, awards the party the experience earned from everyone knocked out during the boarding, sends the boarding party's crew back to their ship, leaves combat, and moves the player back to the zone the boarding started from. It does nothing at all if no boarding is in progress.

globalTriggers.notes: Fleeing or a forced end to combat does not count as a win, so neither raises this. Its 'fires immediately on entering the zone' and 'only fires once' settings are written out in the source but are set to the values they already have.

globalTriggers.name: tEndBoarding_combatLost
globalTriggers.summary: Ends a boarding fight the moment the boarders lose it.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when combat is lost in a zone that carries this trigger. The boarding-deck setup puts it there: 'tEnterBoardingZone' copies this trigger into the deck zone shortly after the deck loads, so losing the fight on the deck ends the boarding. A trigger only reacts to a lost battle once it belongs to the current zone, so on its own, as a global trigger, it never fires from the battle result.
firedBy: The engine, when a battle is lost in a zone that carries this trigger
'tEnterBoardingZone', which copies this trigger into the boarding-deck zone
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Ends the boarding: blackens the screen, drowns any hostile boarders left in the water once no fighters remain, awards the party the experience earned from everyone knocked out during the boarding, sends the boarding party's crew back to their ship, leaves combat, and moves the player back to the zone the boarding started from. It does nothing at all if no boarding is in progress.

globalTriggers.notes: A defeat only counts here if combat ended on its own; a combat that the game forces to an end, including the one the boarding timeout itself causes, does not raise this. Its 'fires immediately on entering the zone' and 'only fires once' settings are written out in the source but are set to the values they already have.

globalTriggers.name: t_travel_gVars
globalTriggers.summary: Sends the player back to the overworld spot they were standing on before a fleet battle.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Nothing in the engine fires this trigger on its own. In the shipped game a dialog effect fires it at the end of a fleet battle, to put the player back where the battle interrupted them. It can equally be fired by another trigger, an action, or a user-interface command.
firedBy: Dialog effects that name 't_travel_gVars', as the game's own fleet-battle wrap-up dialog does
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Actions, via an effect that raises the trigger actor value with this trigger's name

effects.description: A tenth of a second after this trigger fires, travels the player to the zone named by the global variable 'playerPrevZone', at the tile given by the global variables 'playerX' and 'playerY', facing rotation 90, with no autosave taken on arrival. If the game is in combat when this runs it instead asks the player whether they want to flee combat to that destination, and if an action is being resolved it does nothing. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left before the delay elapses.

globalTriggers.notes: The three global variables it reads are written by the engine when a fleet battle starts, so firing this without a fleet battle having happened sends the player to wherever those variables were last left.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterProcZone
globalTriggers.summary: Covers the arrival in every procedurally generated room with a short screen fade.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires as soon as a procedurally generated zone has finished loading, before the player takes a step, and regardless of where in the room they stand. Every procedurally generated zone gets a copy of this trigger built into it automatically, so a modder never has to attach it. It is skipped when a zone is entered through the debug console.
firedBy: Every procedurally generated zone, which is given a copy of this trigger as it is built
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Plays the short screen-blackening effect. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position and covers the whole view while the new room appears.

globalTriggers.notes: This is the one global trigger the engine attaches to zones by itself, so changing its effects changes what happens on entering every procedurally generated room in the game. Marking it as firing immediately on zone entry also means walking into its area can never fire it.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterPort
globalTriggers.summary: Runs the whole arrival-at-a-port sequence: the loading fade, the port name banner, refreshing the hires and shop owners, and the port's greeting dialog.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the player docks at a port. Every port zone in the game carries its own entry trigger whose effect names 'tEnterPort', so it goes off as the player steps into the port. It is not fired by any engine call site of its own.
firedBy: Port zones, whose entry trigger names 'tEnterPort'
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Plays the loading screen-blackening effect. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position and covers the whole view while the port loads in.

Half a second in, fires the trigger 'tTextOverlayPopup_port', which slides the port's name and flag banner down over the top of the screen and then slides it away again. Only that trigger's requirement formula is checked, so it is not blocked by having already run in this zone. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, fires the trigger 'tDespawnHires', which clears out the port's rotating cast of hireable characters if enough time has passed since the last visit. Only that trigger's requirement formula is checked. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

Just after the despawn, fires the trigger 'tSpawnHires', which populates the port with a fresh set of hireable characters when its conditions are met. Only that trigger's requirement formula is checked. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

Also fires the trigger 'tUpdateMyPort', which levels up the port's shopkeepers and collects the takings from a port the player owns. Only that trigger's requirement formula is checked. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A fifth of a second in, looks for a dialog registered to override the slot named 'enterPort' whose requirement passes, and either starts that conversation or, if it has no lines of its own, just runs its effects. This is the hook a mod uses to make a crew member speak up on arriving at a port. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, throws away the saved interior layout of every ship in the player's fleet, so the decks are rebuilt undamaged the next time anyone boards them. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, adds one to the global variable 'portsEntered', the running count of port visits. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.notes: None of its flags are changed from their defaults, so a zone that carries a copy of it flags that copy as done on entering the zone; in the shipped game it is always reached through a zone trigger's trigger effect, which bypasses that check and consults only the requirement formula.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterLoc
globalTriggers.summary: Gives crew members a chance to speak up when the party lands at an out-of-the-way location.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the player arrives at a non-port location such as a beach, farm or swamp landing. Those zones carry their own entry trigger whose effect names 'tEnterLoc', so it goes off as the party steps ashore. It is not fired by any engine call site of its own.
firedBy: Landing-site zones, whose entry trigger names 'tEnterLoc'
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Looks for a dialog registered to override the slot named 'enterLoc' whose requirement passes, and either starts that conversation or, if it has no lines of its own, just runs its effects. Nothing happens when no registered dialog qualifies. This is the hook a mod uses to make a companion comment on arriving somewhere.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterZone
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs every time the player finishes moving into a new zone, so content can react to any zone change.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires at the end of setting up a newly loaded zone, once its actors and lighting are in place, with the player as the triggering actor. It is skipped while a saved game is being loaded, so it does not go off on the zone the player is restored into. Only its requirement formula is consulted, so it is not blocked by the once-per-zone done list and it fires on every zone change.
firedBy: The engine, when a newly loaded zone has finished being set up
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it and have them run on every zone entry. It fires after the zone's own entry triggers have been dealt with.

globalTriggers.name: tExitZone
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs every time the player leaves a zone, so content can react to any zone change.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires while the current zone is being torn down and before the new one begins loading, after tiles have reacted to being left behind but before the game autosaves its working state and clears its pending timers. The player is the triggering actor, and only its requirement formula is consulted, so it is not blocked by the once-per-zone done list and it fires on every zone change.
firedBy: The engine, when the player leaves a zone
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it. Take care with delayed effects here: pending delayed effects are thrown away moments later as part of the zone change, so anything with a delay attached to this trigger will never run.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterGrove
globalTriggers.summary: Runs on arriving in a grove: offers a companion remark and then repaints the grove's foliage to suit the part of the world it sits in.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires the moment a grove finishes generating, before the player takes a step and regardless of where in the grove they stand. Grove level data lists this trigger among the triggers it wants, so every generated grove carries a copy of it.
firedBy: Grove zones, whose level data lists 'tEnterGrove' among its triggers
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Looks for a dialog registered to override the slot named 'enterGrove' whose requirement passes, and either starts that conversation or, if it has no lines of its own, just runs its effects. Nothing happens when no registered dialog qualifies.

Fires 'tEnterGroveDecorate1', which recolours the grove's grass for the north-west of the world map, but only when this grove's location sits west of world column 300 and north of world row 400. The condition is a gate on this effect itself: when it fails the effect is skipped and the rest of the list still runs.

Fires 'tEnterGroveDecorate2', a different grass recolouring, but only when this grove's location sits west of world column 300 and south of world row 600. The condition is a gate on this effect itself: when it fails the effect is skipped and the rest of the list still runs.

Fires 'tEnterGroveDecorate3', a third grass and dirt recolouring, but only when this grove's location sits east of world column 400 and north of world row 150. The condition is a gate on this effect itself: when it fails the effect is skipped and the rest of the list still runs.

globalTriggers.notes: The three decorating conditions do not cover the whole map, so a grove outside all three regions simply keeps its default colours. A zone that already has a trigger of its own with one of these names wins over the global one of the same name. Marking this trigger as firing immediately on zone entry also means walking into its area can never fire it.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterGroveDecorate1
globalTriggers.summary: Repaints a grove's grass in the pale palette used for the north-west of the world map.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires only when something names it. In the shipped game that is 'tEnterGrove', which fires it on arriving in a grove whose location lies west of world column 300 and north of world row 400. Nothing in the engine fires it directly.
firedBy: 'tEnterGrove', which fires it for groves in the north-west of the world map
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Switches the current zone's ordinary grass colours over to the palette 'overworld2'. Every grass tile in the zone is drawn in the new colours from now on.
Switches the current zone's shadowed grass colours over to the palette 'overworld3', so shaded grass matches the recoloured lit grass.
Sweeps every tile in the zone and removes any copies of the placeholder junk item. Since no tile coordinate is given, the sweep covers the whole zone rather than a single tile.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterGroveDecorate2
globalTriggers.summary: Repaints a grove's grass in the palette used for the south-west of the world map.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires only when something names it. In the shipped game that is 'tEnterGrove', which fires it on arriving in a grove whose location lies west of world column 300 and south of world row 600. Nothing in the engine fires it directly.
firedBy: 'tEnterGrove', which fires it for groves in the south-west of the world map
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it

effects.description: Switches the current zone's ordinary grass colours over to the palette 'overworld4'. Every grass tile in the zone is drawn in the new colours from now on.
Switches the current zone's shadowed grass colours over to the palette 'overworld6', so shaded grass matches the recoloured lit grass.
Sweeps every tile in the zone and removes any copies of the placeholder junk item. Since no tile coordinate is given, the sweep covers the whole zone rather than a single tile.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterGroveDecorate3
globalTriggers.summary: Repaints a grove's grass and bare earth in the palette used for the far north-east of the world map.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires only when something names it. In the shipped game that is 'tEnterGrove', which fires it on arriving in a grove whose location lies east of world column 400 and north of world row 150. Nothing in the engine fires it directly.
firedBy: 'tEnterGrove', which fires it for groves in the far north-east of the world map
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Switches the current zone's ordinary grass colours over to the palette 'p65'. Every grass tile in the zone is drawn in the new colours from now on.
Switches the current zone's shadowed grass colours over to the palette 'overworld11', so shaded grass matches the recoloured lit grass.
Switches the current zone's bare-earth colours over to the palette 'p26', so paths and clearings match the recoloured grass.
Sweeps every tile in the zone and removes any copies of the placeholder junk item. Since no tile coordinate is given, the sweep covers the whole zone rather than a single tile.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterDojo
globalTriggers.summary: Sets up a dojo sparring match: locks the controls, trims the party down to the landing party, clears lingering effects, and drops everyone into combat two seconds later.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the player walks into the sparring area of a dojo. Each dojo zone carries its own trigger over that area whose effect names 'tEnterDojo'. It is not fired by any engine call site of its own.
firedBy: Dojo zones, whose sparring-area trigger names 'tEnterDojo'
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: Locks the player out of acting for two seconds while the match is set up. This sets the lockout outright rather than extending an existing one, so a longer lockout already running is cut short to two seconds.
Plays the brief screen-blackening effect. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position and covers the whole view.

Two seconds after this trigger fires, starts combat with a battlefield radius of 9999, which takes in the entire dojo and everyone in it. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left before the delay elapses. Its delay also means the two effects listed after it actually happen before it does.
Removes from the zone every party member who is not part of the landing party, so only the crew the player chose to bring ashore take part in the sparring.
Casts the game's zone-wide dispel on the triggering actor's tile, stripping temporary effects off everything within 99 tiles, so nobody walks into the match still carrying buffs from outside.

globalTriggers.notes: The effects do not all happen in the order they are listed: the combat effect carries a two-second delay, so trimming the party and dispelling the zone both happen first, immediately when the trigger fires.

globalTriggers.name: tEnterOverworld
globalTriggers.summary: Settles the player back onto the open sea: ocean ambience, the nearest port's theme, any treasure they were told about, and an autosave.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the player returns to the overworld map from somewhere else. The overworld zone carries its own trigger whose effect names 'tEnterOverworld'. It is not fired by any engine call site of its own.
firedBy: The overworld zone, whose entry trigger names 'tEnterOverworld'
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: A tenth of a second in, plays one of the randomised ocean ambience sounds, fading it in and out. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, starts playing the outdoor theme belonging to whichever location on the map lies nearest the player, so the music reflects the region they are sailing in. Nothing happens if there is no location nearby. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, if a treasure spot has been marked on the map, buries a shipwreck at that spot stocked with gold, lost cargo, two pieces of random loot and a set of lost documents, then clears the mark so it is not placed twice. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, sweeps the whole map and removes every shipwreck whose container has been emptied out, so looted wrecks disappear rather than littering the sea. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

Almost immediately, fires the trigger 'tOverworldAutosave', which takes an autosave if the game has been told one is due. Only that trigger's requirement formula is checked, so it is not blocked by having already run in this zone. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.notes: Because the autosave effect has a shorter delay than the four before it, it is the first of the five to actually happen.

globalTriggers.name: tOverworldAutosave
globalTriggers.summary: Takes a one-shot autosave when the player returns to the open sea after an event that asked for one.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when 'tEnterOverworld' runs on returning to the overworld map, but only when the global variable 'autosaveInOverworld' has been set, which is how an event such as the end of a fleet battle asks for a save on the way out. Nothing in the engine fires it directly.
firedBy: 'tEnterOverworld', which fires it a hundredth of a second after the player reaches the open sea
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: A second after this trigger fires, marks an autosave as due. The save is not taken there and then: the game waits until it is out of combat, nothing is acting, the player is not locked out of interacting, and no tile effects are pending, then flashes 'Autosaved!' on screen and writes the autosave. Hardcore mode suppresses the save. Because this effect is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.
Clears the global variable 'autosaveInOverworld' back to 0, so the next return to the open sea does not save again until something asks for it. No value is supplied, so the variable is set to zero.

globalTriggers.notes: The clearing of the request variable happens straight away while the save itself is a second later, so the request is consumed even if the save is postponed.

globalTriggers.name: tLoadOverworld
globalTriggers.summary: Restores the sea ambience and regional music when a saved game is loaded onto the open sea.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when a saved game is loaded and the player is restored onto the overworld map. The overworld zone carries a trigger that reacts to a game being loaded and names 'tLoadOverworld'. It does the sound half of what 'tEnterOverworld' does, without the treasure, cleanup or autosave steps, because loading a save should not change the world. It is not fired by any engine call site of its own.
firedBy: The overworld zone, whose game-loaded trigger names 'tLoadOverworld'
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects

effects.description: A tenth of a second in, plays one of the randomised ocean ambience sounds, fading it in and out. No tile is given, so it is queued at the camera's own position. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A tenth of a second in, starts playing the outdoor theme belonging to whichever location on the map lies nearest the player, so the music matches the region the save was made in. Nothing happens if there is no location nearby. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.name: tLoadGame
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs once when a saved game is loaded, so content can set itself up on resume.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires at the end of loading a saved game, after the saved zone has been rebuilt and the party put back in it, with the player as the triggering actor. It is skipped when the loaded state is the main menu backdrop or a brand-new game, so it marks a genuine resume rather than any zone setup.
firedBy: The engine, when a saved game has finished loading
Other triggers, via a trigger effect that names it
Dialog effects
globalTriggers.notes: Ships with no effects at all. It exists purely so that a mod can add trigger effects to it and have them run whenever a save is resumed. Unlike most trigger dispatches this one does not check the trigger's requirement formula first, so any gating must be done on the effects themselves.

globalTriggers.name: tNewDay
globalTriggers.summary: Empty hook that runs once at the start of each in-game day, so content can attach daily upkeep.
globalTriggers.whenFired: Fires when the world clock rolls over into a new day, after the day's own housekeeping has been done: the weather has changed, the crew have eaten and been paid, morale has been adjusted and every port's market rates have been recalculated. The player is the triggering actor, and only the requirement formula is consulted, so it is not blocked by the once-per-zone done list and it fires again every day.

effects.description: Locks the player out of acting for two seconds while the journal presentation plays. This sets the lockout outright rather than extending an existing one, so a longer lockout already running is cut short to two seconds.

Writes the goal 'Hire a party of 5 crew.' into the first free journal goal slot, quietly: no journal is opened and no flash or chime is played, because the journal is opened deliberately a moment later. A goal with the same text already in the journal is not added twice.

A second and a half in, opens the journal at its first page with its buttons still available, so the player sees the goal that was just written. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

A second and a half in, sets the global variable 'hireCrewGoalDone' to 1, which is what stops this trigger's requirement from passing a second time. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

Two seconds in, strikes the goal 'Hire a party of 5 crew.' off the journal, turning to its page, flashing the line and playing the quest-completed chime. Nothing happens if no open goal with that text is found. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.notes: The goal text is matched by its exact wording, so the text in the effect that adds the goal and the one that completes it must stay identical for the completion to find it. The two-second interaction lockout covers the whole sequence, which ends with the completion effect at exactly two seconds.

This effect is written as a whole task line rather than a task name plus fields, so it takes its numbers from the line itself and none of the effect's own value, coordinate, flag or requirement fields apply. effects.description: Sends the party from the location back out to the map tile the location sits on, with no offset applied. If the game is in combat this instead asks whether the player wants to flee out of the location, and if an action is resolving it does nothing. An autosave is taken on arrival.

globalTriggers.notes: Its tile coordinate is set to 0,0 in two separate statements right after the trigger is created; those zeroes are the destination offset from the location's own map tile, so the party lands exactly on it.

globalTriggers.notes: The order here is deliberate and fragile: the departure carries a small delay so that it is safely queued before the enemy check can abandon the rest of the list. Removing that delay would let the check cancel the departure as well.

A fifth of a second in, plays the high humming sound on every party member's position, accompanying the closing-gate visual. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.notes: Nearly every effect here is rewritten at runtime before the trigger fires, so the values recorded are starting points rather than what actually plays. The screen effects have their positions replaced with the centre of the screen, or a quarter of the monitor size when a maximise is pending; the backdrop zone and its vertical position are replaced with the ship from the most recent save; the two character placements are filled in with that save's crew, and are blanked first so an unreadable save leaves them empty; the weather and darkness colour are swapped for clear skies and a lighter tint once the extra options are unlocked; and the maximise flag is set only on the first play of the intro. The delays put the effects in a different order from the list: the window maximise comes first, then the gate animation, then the backdrop and its crew, the weather and lighting, and finally the menu itself.

The last of these repeats begins 163 seconds in, so the loop as a whole runs to about 171 seconds.

At 171 seconds, loads an empty backdrop at the top-left corner, which clears the port scene away behind the blackout. Because it is delayed it is queued rather than run on the spot, and it is dropped without running if the zone is left first.

globalTriggers.notes: This is by far the longest trigger in the game, and its effect list is not written out one effect at a time: the middle of it, the tour of the twenty-one ports, is generated by a loop and is recorded here as a single summarised entry rather than the hundred and five separate effects it really produces. Everything is driven by delays measured from the moment it fires, so the list order says almost nothing about the order things happen; the delays run from one second up to 222. The opening interaction lock of 226 seconds is what keeps the player out of it from start to finish, so shortening the sequence without shortening that lock leaves the player stuck watching nothing.
